While leaders are looked up to by people all around the world, some leaders might have completely different world views and policies. But, after looking for similarities in the greatest leaders in history, they all share some of the same qualities. In my opinion, a leader's most important and defining qualities are their ability to be inspiring, fair, and intelligent. Having those traits is important because they help leaders keep their people happy, their society united, and prevent external threats. 

Firstly, being an inspiring leader is important because they keep their people happy and motivated. For example, during Obama's presidential run, he inspired people by forming his campaign around the hopes of Americans. This can be seen with his famous quote "Yes we can." in response to people doubting his ability to reform the country. Furthermore, whenever Obama had a democratic supporting rally, the people there were always seen with a smile on their face and happy to support Obama. As seen with Obama's presidential platform and rallies, the result of being inspirational is that it keeps people happy and motivated to support their leaders.

Secondly, being a fair leader is crucial because it ensures justice is unbiased which leads to their society being united. For example, fair leaders will always investigate corruption. Imagine a high ranking member of the government being corrupt and the people protested. If the leader of the government was fair, they would immediately take action against the corrupt official leading to the people being appeased. But if they weren't fair, the people would notice that corruption was not being punished which might lead to a revolution started by the people. So in order for a society to remain united, its leaders must be fair to make sure their followers don't get mad at them and their system.

Lastly, a leader being intelligent helps to keep their society or country safe from threats. For instance, Canada spends a lot of money on military intelligence gathering in order to keep its citizens safe. But it is ultimately up to the higher ranking military officials and politicians to decide what to do with the information. If the higher ups are intelligent, they would know exactly what is going on in the world and how to best use their assets in order to combat known and unknown threats. But if the officials didn't have a complete world view, they might not know the threat was important enough to investigate immediately. If the threat was serious enough, it might grow out of hand and directly affect their country's citizens. Therefore, just like military officials, leaders must be intelligent enough in order to protect their people to the best of their ability. 

To conclude, I think the most important qualities of a leader are their ability to be inspiring, fair, and intelligent. Having those important traits helps keep their people happy, their country united, and their society safe from external harm.

In my opinion, I believe the three most important qualities and traits of a leader are adaptability, assertiveness, and empathy .

Leaders should be able to adapt to their surroundings, and the people they work with. As the world is a constantly changing, evolving place, leaders should be able to adapt, problem solve, and figure out what to do in many different types of situations. Problems will always occur, anticipated for or not, they are unavoidable. Leaders should be able to adapt to these problems or situations, and figure out how to solve them in a quick, effective manner. For example, say a recently hired manager was hired in a new building, meeting new people, and having new problems. This manager should be able to adapt to their new surroundings, and help solve the issues going on throughout the office. Without being able to adapt to their new environment, the manager may struggle to help solve the different problems throughout the office, or help their peers.

Secondly, being assertive is essential for getting a point across, which is what leaders will have to do constantly. Without being assertive, it is very easy for team mates to diminish what their leader is saying, and not take the leader seriously. Say for example, there is a group project that a team must complete with a certain deadline. Bob, the team leader, notices that his peers have not done their portion of a team project, and have spent their time goofing around. In order for Bob to get his point across, he must be assertive with his reasoning. If not, his peers may not take Bob's warnings seriously, and ignore him. Being assertive will allow leaders to get their point across in a serious, effective, and respectable manner.

Finally, having empathy as a leader is a very important trait to have. Being an empathetic leader allows you to understand your teammates perspectives better, allowing you to build trust between them, vital for teamwork. Understanding your teammates, peers, or anyone a leader may be working with allows them to see many different perspectives,  work around them, and help each other out. For example, a teacher is grading science tests, and notices a student has gotten a significantly lower grade than their usual average. The teacher has also noticed that the student is going through a rough patch at home. Instead of assuming the student did not study, the teacher understands how the student is feeling, and asks the student if they need help. This shows that the teacher understands the student, and is empathetic towards them. This will further build trust between the student and the teacher. This is just one example, however understanding others will build trust, let leaders work around different situations, and help out their teammates.

In conclusion, being a leader requires many different traits and qualities. The three traits I believe to be the most important are adaptability, confidence, and empathy.

The most important qualities of a leader consist of three main points: patience, social skills and a hardworking attitude. This essay will discuss how these qualities can help in work and school scenarios.

Patience is the first skill a leader needs. Why? to start, leaders work with many people and need to be able to remain calm when there are mistakes and setbacks. This way there is less time spent panicking and more time spent solving problems.For example there is a story of a couple who started a contracting and renovation firm together and one of the many setbacks they encountered was a incorrect order placement by one of their employee's which caused problems with the client and set them back in their schedule. Patience helped this couple to move on from their employee's mistake so that they could fix the issue, explain things to the client, find another use for the wrong order and quickly receive the correct order and eventually, setting everything back on track.

The second most vital quality every leader needs is good social skills which allows a leader to properly communicate with their team and get things done. This quality was perfectly demonstrated in a daycare centre where a new CEO had just finished hiring all her staff and was ready to open her doors. She obviously held regular meetings to make sure there were no problems with any of the staff, but she also made a point of checking in on each room everyday to make sure everything ran smoothly and that her employee's felt comfortable speaking to her. Because of this CEO's good social skills and proper connections to her team, she was instantly alerted when a problem arose with one of the children. Instead of being scared to admit something had gone wrong, the employee felt safe which allowed for quick response time and even faster problem resolution.

The final quality of a leader is a hard working attitude. Being a leader is about more than telling others what to do, it is about setting a good example and being able to accomplish things yourself. During a group project among the student council during a particularly busy year, there was a student who was leading the council and helped make choices but they never simply told other what to do and then supervised, they constantly helped with each and every department to make sure all deadlines were met. Even though being the student council leader truly only meant overseeing and making sure things were completed on time, this student showed a hardworking attitude and worked wherever there was a need. Because of that students hard work, all of the events planned by the student council that were very successful, lucrative and fun.

In conclusion the three most important qualities of a leader are patience, social skills and a hardworking attitude because those are the skills that allow you to look past mistakes, communicate with your team and complete tasks on time.

Being a great leader requires you to be able to take charge in any circumstance. If you are in a group with other people, whether you know them or not, it is good to be able to take charge, as the others may not be willing to. Taking charge could be making decisions about who does what in a project, it could be guiding everyone on a trail or path, or it could be as small as choosing where to eat with friends. No matter how big or small the group is or how major or unimportant the decision is, it is an important leadership skill to be able to take charge. While taking charge is important, so is the ability to take advice and criticism and use it effectively.

It is also important to be able to take criticism or advice if you want to be a good leader. Taking criticism is harder for most people than taking charge, so it is important to not take charge if you are unable to also take criticism without getting upset. While it is the least important aspect, it is important to be able to make quick and thoughtful decisions.

Being a leader is more than just taking charge, it also requires you to be able to quick decisions and good decisions. If you are the leader of a group and you are in a bad situation, your quick decision could be the difference between life and death for your group. Although making quick decisions is a great skill to have, it is more important to be able to make quick decisions that are good. Making great decisions is important, but is the least important skill for being a leader. It is still possible to be a good leader, as you hopefully won't have to make quick decisions too often. Although it isn't the most important, it is the difference between a good leader and a great leader.

They would need to ensure the well-being of their group and provide them with reassurance whenever it's required. To be a leader, some qualities are more important than others. The most important and ideal qualities of a leader would be: honesty, support, determination/dedication and loyalty.  

As a leader, it's one's responsibility to ensure the well-being of the group they lead. To do this, they need to be honest. If someone is doing something wrong, or something that will be bad for them, it's the leader's job to inform the person with pure honesty that their actions are not ideal ( ex. when a person decides to put down another person, instead of staying quiet, the leader should step up and tell them that their actions are wrong with pure honesty). 

Along with that, support is another important quality in a leader as it's their job to confirm that their group receives the help that they need. To be supportive, the leader should always help out their members no matter what and find solutions to problems ( ex. If a member is unsure of something, it's the leader's responsibility to help them distinguish between what's right and wrong in the situation instead of letting them find it out themselves). 

The next quality and in my opinion, the most important quality, is determination/dedication. Every leader would want their group to be the best or better than the others. To do this, they must have the determination to keep their group on top. They should be encouraging to their group, push them to do better but it's also important to make sure that they don't get burnt out. ( ex. To keep their group on top, the leader will go to any extent and also push their group members to put all their effort in by explaining the various benefits of doing so). 

The last ideal quality of a leader is loyalty. It is an extremely important quality to have as a leader and even as a person. The leader of the group can prove their loyalty by always being there for people whenever they need it, never lying to their members even when it seems like that is the easy way out and putting all their effort towards ensuring their group is the best from all aspects. Loyalty is a combination of honesty, support and dedication. 

There are many other qualities that make up the ideal leader, but I believe that these 5 qualities are the most important.

A leader in my personal opinion should be able to tie their shoes, because if your not smart enough to tie your shoes how do you expect to be smart enough to be a leader. A leader should be comfortable with public speaking, because if this leader is a leader of something big like a prime minister or presidant, they will need to be ready to  answer any questions the press might ask. A leader should have a plan to make whatever they are leading better, they should never be satisfied with how they are right now, but they should try and make it even better. A leader should never try and bribe people to become a leader, they can tell the people what their plans are for the future, but never try and bribe them with money, food, etc. A leader should stay true to their word, if they say they will do something they need to do it, not say something then do the complete opposite. Those are some of the quilities I have for a leader.
